title: Improve reproducible seeding and sampled distributed tracing in load harness
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: The load/perf harness experiences intermittent flakiness when running long tail scenarios on CI and in the perf-cluster. Two root causes were identified: (1) non-deterministic RNG/seed propagation across worker shards causing variation in generated sequences and cache warmup, and (2) noisy distributed tracing (trace sampling at 0.1) that makes post-run timeline analysis unreliable for low-frequency regressions. Both reduce our ability to reproduce regressions and increase time-to-debug for serving runtime and scheduling changes.

Goal: Implement deterministic seeding across runner shards and introduce an adaptive sampling layer for distributed traces that preserves low-frequency error traces while keeping storage/ingest costs stable. This ticket refactors the harness bootstrap to centralize seeding and adds a trace-sampling shim and config flags for per-run sampling policy. We will also add a reproducibility smoke check to CI so any change that changes RNG or shuffle behavior must be approved.

Scope (what this ticket covers):
- Centralize RNG seed generation in the harness coordinator and propagate seeds to Docker/Pod worker processes via env var and explicit seed artifact.
- Add optional prefix/KV-caching deterministic warmup mode for long-sequence scenarios.
- Implement an adaptive trace-sampling middleware that uses reservoir sampling + priority for error/slow requests and exposes per-run sampling policy (fixed, adaptive, full).
- Add CI smoke test that runs 3 seeded runs and asserts identical token-count and KV-cache hit patterns for base scenarios.
- Update docs + runbook and instrument metrics for sampled-trace drop rate and cross-run variance.

Out of scope: full rewrite of loadgen (separate ticket) and rewriting model sharding layer.
acceptance_criteria: Harness coordinator emits a deterministic seed artifact (sha256) for each run and all workers receive the same seed via env var and --seed CLI flag.
Three CI smoke runs (seeded) for the standard long-tail scenario produce identical sequence checksums and cache-warm histogram equality within 0% tolerance.
Adaptive trace-sampling middleware implemented and enabled behind feature flag; default sampling policy set to 'adaptive' for nightly perf runs.
Dashboard panels added: 'trace-sampling rate', 'sampled-error-trace-count', 'cross-run token-count variance' and visible to SRE and Perf teams.
Documentation (Confluence) updated with runbook for reproducing flakiness and a checklist for seed-breaking changes.
No customer-facing behavior changes; customer_impact set to 'low'.

Approach A is simpler for Kubernetes but artifact approach gives better audit trail. Leaning toward A for MVP, will add artifact write for audit if time permits.

notes_on_risks_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs: Full-trace capture (sampling=full) would make debugging easier but would raise ingestion costs and slow analysis. Adaptive sampling tries to keep the most valuable traces while keeping costs bounded. Risk if RNG change exists in deep dependency (third-party loadgen) — mitigation: CI smoke to block merges. Workarounds: policy to pin dependency or vendor a small wrapper module.
runbook_quick_commands:
# reproduce locally
# 1) start coordinator with SEED=12345
# 2) run 'python -m perf_harness.coordinator --seed 12345 --scenario long_tail'
# 3) collect worker logs and compare 'run-checksum' lines

# check trace sampling config
curl -s http://<harness-host>/_debug/sampling-config
